packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-14 — unverified image reading

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading. Blind reading. I have not tried to identify work or author. (The images themselves show a library stamp and pencil numbers, recorded below as visible marks only.)

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Two different faces are shown: image-001 (overview) with tiles image-002 (upper) and image-003 (lower) = "face 1"; image-004 (overview) with tiles image-005 (upper) and image-006 (lower) = "face 2".

FACE 1 — observations
- A parchment leaf lying against the inside of a board (red-brown leather turn-ins visible at bottom and right; gutter at left): it appears to be used as a pastedown. Text upright, one column of long lines, 21 lines of text plus one rubric line inside the block and a second, very faint red line below the last text line.
- Left edge is in the gutter/trimmed: one to five letters are missing at the start of most lines. Right edge is overlapped by a second, separate parchment strip, so the last one to four letters of most lines are covered or lost. A paper/parchment repair patch and brown stain obscure the middle of lines 1-3.
- Script: a rounded, well-spaced minuscule with "&"-ligature, e-caudata (ę), tall s, uncial-type capitals touched with orange-red at sentence openings (A of "Adde", N of "Novemb", A of "Annus", S of "Superat", S of "Sed"). Roman numerals between points, with superscript endings (ma, na, or, mo).
- One rubric in orange-red rustic/square capitals inside the block (line 8) and a second faint orange-red line after the last line; both abraded.
- One interlinear gloss in small letters above line 18 (above "adimitur").
- A violet octagonal ink stamp in the lower margin reading "BIBLIOTHECA PALAT. VINDOBONENSIS."
- The separate strip at the right carries writing in a different, later-looking, more angular hand in red-brown ink, running at 180 degrees to the main text (upside down in this view), about 20 line-fragments, each only a few letters wide.
- At the far left of image-001 a sliver of the facing page with a few letters is visible; not readable.

FACE 1 — tentative interpretation
- Reckoning prose about months, "regulares", moon and "epactae" (calendar computation), divided into sections by red titles. The upside-down strip looks like a binding reinforcement cut from another manuscript; unrelated to the main text as far as I can see.

FACE 2 — observations
- A page (leaf edge and book block visible at right, gutter at left) with ruled lines, carrying several short, unrelated entries in at least four different hands and inks, with blank or erased intervals: it has the look of a flyleaf or originally blank page used for pen trials and notes.
- Top margin: pencil "2723" (left), the same violet stamp "BIBLIOTHECA PALAT. VINDOBONENSIS." (centre), and a pencil note at right of which I read "[illegible] 1350 Bll"? ; a small pencil stroke/"1" in the top right corner.
- Entry (a): two lines in a cursive hand, dark ink. Then three ruled lines with erased or rubbed writing, the third showing a faint trial of the same words as entry (b).
- Entry (b): two lines in red-brown ink in a rounder, earlier-looking book hand, with a large initial T and a row of neumes (musical signs) above the first words only.
- Entry (c): two lines, cursive, a dated note.
- Entry (d): three lines in the same or a similar cursive; entry (e): two lines; entry (f): four lines in a larger, bolder cursive, the last two with pen-flourished initials in the margin.
- No rubrics, running titles or glosses.

2. SPANS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected and transcribed: all 21 text lines and the first rubric of face 1; all legible entries of face 2.
Unread: (i) the upside-down strip at the right of face 1 — I did not rotate the image and the fragments are a few letters each; a rotated crop is needed; (ii) the second, faint red rubric at the foot of face 1 (only scattered letters); (iii) the erased lines on face 2; (iv) the sliver of the facing page at the left of image-001.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: ( ) = expansion; [lost] = letters hidden in gutter, under the right-hand strip or under the patch; ę = e-caudata; & = et-ligature as written; superscripts shown with ^.

FACE 1 — image-002 (upper tile; lines counted from top of image-002)

image-002 L1:  [lost]. Sept(ember) hab& dies .xxx. secundu(m) solem? [under patch]. Adde suos re[lost]
image-002 L2:  [lost]res .v. fiunt .xxx.v. ipse hab&? [under patch] lunam? .xxx. Equato
image-002 L3:  [lost]m. idest luna(m). & dies sup(ra)dictos? [partly under patch]. & remanent .v. Oc[lost]
image-002 L4:  Octob(er) hab& dies .xxx.i. Adde suos regulares .v. fiunt .xxx[lost]
image-002 L5:  [lost]uato eos cum luna .xx^ma. viiii^na. remanent .vii. Novemb(er) .vii[lost]
image-002 L6:  [lost]ter de ceteris age. Ideo autem annum solarem p(er) xxx[lost]
image-002 L7:  [lost]dere iussimus. quia lunea ultra hunc modum minime con[lost]
image-002 L8:  [lost]ttur. [RUBRIC, orange-red capitals, abraded:] ANNOS? [gap] EXTENDUNTUR? DE EPACTIS LUNAE CU[lost]
image-002 L9:  [lost]rimo anno circuli decennovenalis. nullę sunt epactę. Id[lost]
image-002 L10: [lost]o in k(alendis). septembribus .v. est luna. In k(alendis). octobribus .v. In k(alendis)[lost]
image-002 L11: [lost]embribus .vii. & reliquis kalendis. iuxta ipsos regulares
image-002 L12: [lost]do autem anno .xi. sunt epactę quę de anno solari veniu[lost]
image-002 L13: Annus solaris hab& dies .ccc.lx.v. Superat annum luna[lost]
image-002 L14: [lost] hab& .ccc.l.iiii^or. dies .xi. diebus. & ita p(er) singulos annos .x[lost]   (bottom of tile; = image-003 L4)

FACE 1 — image-003 (lower tile; lines counted from top of image-003). image-003 L1-L4 repeat image-002 L11-L14 (overlap, not additional text).

image-003 L1:  = image-002 L11
image-003 L2:  = image-002 L12
image-003 L3:  = image-002 L13
image-003 L4:  = image-002 L14
image-003 L5:  [lost]ens. cum usq(ue) ad xxx. p(er)veneris tollens .xxx. quot rem[lost]
image-003 L6:  [lost]nt epactas habebis. Sed hoc nobis nimium necesse est
image-003 L7:  [lost]inisse. ut ultimo. idest .xviiii^mo anno .xii. addas idest co[lost]
image-003 L8:  [lost]os? xi. & unum qui lunę in suo saltu adimitur. Eodem qu[lost]
              [interlinear gloss above "adimitur", small letters:] in zogan vuirdit
image-003 L9:  anno lunea novembris mensis. quę ceteris annis .xxx.
image-003 L10: [lost] habere dinoscitur .xx.viiii. dies solummodo hab&.
image-003 L11: [lost]s saltum de xx. nona in primam & pretermittens.
image-003 L12: [RUBRIC, orange-red, very faint and abraded: scattered letters only; I see what may be "… DE REG… …" and a final "&"; not readable]
image-003, below L12: violet stamp "BIBLIOTHECA PALAT. VINDOBONENSIS."

Notes face 1:
- L1-L3: the patch hides the centre; "solem", "habet lunam" and "supradictos" are read from the tops and tails of letters showing around and through it and are uncertain.
- L4: after "dies" the numeral is ".xxx.i." (thirty plus one stroke); a small flaw follows "xxx".
- L7 and L9: the word is written "lunea" with what may be a correction/ligature at "-ea" (possibly "luna" altered, or "lunae"); I transcribe the letters I see.
- L8 rubric: letter-forms are narrow capitals; the first word could be "ANNOS", "ANNUS" or the end of a longer word; the second "EXTENDUNTUR" is a guess from the surviving strokes "EXTEN…DUN…"; "DE EPACTIS LUNAE" is fairly clear.
- image-003 L8 gloss: the gloss is in a vernacular, not Latin; letters read "in zogan uuirdit" (with double-u), written continuously above "adimitur". I do not interpret it.
- Line beginnings marked [lost] are in the gutter; the missing letters are few (e.g. L9 "[.]rimo", L11 "[…]embribus", L12 "[…]do") but I do not supply them.

RIGHT-HAND STRIP on face 1 (image-002 and image-003, right edge): different hand, written upside down relative to the main text, red-brown ink, about 20 fragments of 3-8 letters. Unread (see above).

FACE 2 — image-005 (upper tile; lines counted from top of image-005)

image-005 L1:  [top margin, modern:] pencil "2723"; violet stamp "BIBLIOTHECA PALAT. VINDOBONENSIS."; pencil "[illegible] 1350 Bll"?
image-005 L2:  Candidior stella me diligit una puella
image-005 L3:  In tota villa no(n) est formosior illa
image-005 L4:  [erased/rubbed line; a few strokes and "…s? te"? at the right end]
image-005 L5:  [erased/rubbed line; "…"]
image-005 L6:  [faint red-brown trial:] Tota p[illegible] es? amica
image-005 L7:  [row of neumes above the next line, over the words "Tota pulchra es amica" only; large initial T begins at this level]
image-005 L8:  Tota pulchra es amica mea & macula non est in te. Favus distil-
image-005 L9:  lans labia tua mel & lac sub lingua tua odor ungentor(um)
image-005 L10: Anno domini Mill(es)imo Trecentesimo lxxii? in die Antonii conf(essoris) p[illegible: "pmdnus"/"p(re)b(e)nd(a)rius"?]
image-005 L11: fridrici wistalarii? de salczburga? [followed by a pen flourish]
image-005 L12: Clare virginis candide? ecclesia nu(n)c p(re)conia virginitatis mere castitatis
image-005 L13: [cropped at tile edge; = image-006 L4]

FACE 2 — image-006 (lower tile; lines counted from top of image-006). image-006 L1-L3 repeat image-005 L10-L12 (overlap).

image-006 L1:  = image-005 L10 (top cropped)
image-006 L2:  = image-005 L11
image-006 L3:  = image-005 L12
image-006 L4:  honore que luxit et duxit p(ri)ma felix puella (Christ)i cellula fruens gloria
image-006 L5:  clara da virgo celica clara nobis gaudia
image-006 L6:  Veni dilecta mea o katherina sponsa mea veni omnia que petisti
image-006 L7:  pure? impetrasti
image-006 L8:  Fac simus ut rasi d(e) libro sathane blasi
image-006 L9:  Aufferat reatus n(ost)ros petrus kathedratus
image-006 L10: Istas formosas tu scriptor suscipe rosas
image-006 L11: Quas tibi mea p(ro) me mittit dorothea

Notes face 2:
- image-005 L2-L3 and image-006 L8-L11 are rhymed verse lines (internal rhyme stella/puella, villa/illa, rasi/blasi, reatus/kathedratus, formosas/rosas, mea?/dorothea); I transcribe them as lines.
- image-005 L10: the numeral after "Trecentesimo" is "lxx" followed by two minims ("lxxii"), possibly "lxxij"/"lxxiii". The last word of the line is abbreviated with a crossed p and I cannot expand it securely. L11: the second word begins "w" or "v" and ends "-alarii"/"-olarii"; the place-word reads "salczburga"/"salzburgk"; all uncertain in detail.
- image-005 L12: "candide" is written with a suspension I am not sure of ("candide"/"candidi"/"cantat"?).
- image-006 L7: first word "pure" or "p(ro)ue"/"iure"; small and faint.
- image-006 L10-L11: the initials I and Q are large pen-flourished letters standing in the left margin; "Q" is a decorated form and "uas" follows on the line.
- image-006 L11: "mea p(ro) me" — the crossed p could be "p(er)" or "p(ro)"; a faint red offset or erased red word lies under "mittit".

4. LIMITATIONS
- Face 1: line beginnings in the gutter and line ends under the strip are lost; three lines are partly under a patch; two rubrics are abraded; the strip text is unread and needs a rotated crop.
- Face 2: erased entries not recoverable from these images; the dated note has two words I could not resolve.
- The two faces need not belong to the same original leaf or text; the images do not show their relation.
- This is an unverified image reading.

Reader activity: opened PROMPT.md; image-001.jpg through image-006.jpg (all six). packet.json not opened.
